What each task of a bundle has done, and what to do next

Source: R/hpc.R
hpc_status.Rd

Reads the records that the tasks of a bundle written by write_hpc_bundle() have left in its folder results/, and says, for each stage of the run, how many tasks are done, which are not and why, and what to do next. It is run on the cluster by the bundle's script status.sh, and works as well on a copy of the bundle brought back.

Usage

hpc_status(dir = ".")

Arguments

dir

A character string, the folder of the bundle. Defaults to the working folder, which is where status.sh runs it.

Value

A data frame with one row per task, invisibly: its stage ("fit" or "kfold"), task number, model, fold (NA for a fit), status, the reason a task is not done, and the seconds it took. A message summarises it.

Details

A task is "done" when it ended well, "failed" when it ended with an error, whose message is its reason, "started" when it began and has no record of how it ended, "queued" when submit.sh submitted it after its files were last written, so that it waits in the queue, and "not started" otherwise. A task that started and has no record is either still running or was stopped by Slurm before it could write one. Slurm says which in the log it wrote for the task, in the folder logs/, and the reason given is read from it: out of time, out of memory, stopped by Slurm for a reason it gives (a node that failed, say), or cancelled. Slurm's command squeue -u $USER (sq on the clusters of the Alliance) lists the tasks still waiting or running.

When tasks remain to be run, the message gives the command that submits them again, and only them: it leaves out a task that may still be running or that waits in the queue, and a refit whose fit is itself still queued or running, since the refit would start without its fit and fail. A task already done is never run twice.

See also

run_hpc_task(), which runs a task, and collect_hpc(), which assembles the results.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# on the cluster, from the folder of the bundle; status.sh runs the same
hpc_status()
} # }
